_comment: The training course's lessons (MISSION-TRAINING.md, SPEC.md §15; M47). Each lesson is its own small situation and a list of steps, and src/lessons.js lets only what a step lists do anything. `start`: `men` by roster id (`at`, and optionally `ap`, `charges`, `hits`, `hidden`; a man not named is not on the board), `enemies` in the map's own shape, `parachutes` ({ at, unit }), `turn`, `alert`; or, in place of `men`, `drop` (M48b): { run, landings: { man: hex } }, a lesson that starts in the drop, each man down where it says with no scatter. A step: `say`, the pen's line on the board (seven words at most) at hex `at` (or under the man it is about), repeated on the card as TO GO ON; `tell`, the card's words before the step is done: what to do; `then` (M48b, the operator's: do it, see it, then NEXT), the card's words once it is done, while what it did is still on the board: what he is now looking at and the rule in its numbers, with a green NEXT; `ring`, hexes to ring, or "men"; `point`, a part of the page to ring (roster, alert, clock, readout, actions, radio); `allow`: { select: [ids] or true, move: [hexes] or "any", actions: [ids], target: [hexes], endTurn, run, jump }; `until`: what ends the step, one of the kinds listed in src/lessons.js; `mayBeSeen` where being spotted is the lesson; `does`, read only by the test that plays the lesson. The words are placeholders for the operator to reword. `free` (M48f) is a step of the passing-out exercise: no `then`, it runs on into the next, and the umpire says what a thing done would have cost on a real mission; its `does.script` is the playthrough the test makes.

steps.tell: Every mission starts in the aircraft. The dashed line across the map is the drop run: the way the aircraft will fly. Click its name on the map, or press ‘1’.
steps.then: The run is chosen. The marked ground is where the men may come down: the wind, shown by the arrow, carries each man 1 or 2 hexes off the line. A mission has 3 runs to choose from. The practice ground has only this one.

steps.tell: Nothing is settled until the men jump. Press ‘SPACE’, or click the run's name again.
steps.then: All six are down, each standing on his parachute. In a mission the wind decides where each man lands. Today the instructor has.

steps.tell: The list on the right is your six men: each man's name, his job and his skill. Click the top row: Sgt. Holloway, ‘Dutch’. Clicking his counter on the map does the same.
steps.then: Dutch is selected. His row is outlined, his counter is marked on the map, and the figure at the right of his row is his action points (AP) for this turn.

steps.tell: The dial is how alarmed the garrison is: Calm, Suspicious, Alert, Alarmed. A man seen adds 1, a parachute found 1, gunfire 2, an explosion 3. The higher it goes, the further the enemy sees and the harder he looks.

This is the turn number, and the strip beside it is the night running out. A mission ends at dawn, on its last turn. The practice ground has no dawn. ‘KEYBOARD’ lists every key, and ‘?’ is how to play.
The box under the map describes whatever the mouse is on. Move the mouse onto Dutch's counter on the map.
steps.then: That is Dutch's entry: his job, his AP, what he carries. Hover an enemy, a piece of ground or a target, and the box describes that instead.

steps.tell: Every man lands on his parachute, and it stays where he landed. Click Barrow.
steps.then: Barrow is selected. The small canopy at the corner of his counter is his parachute, on the ground under him. A second parachute lies by the road, where Vance landed.

steps.tell: A man standing on a parachute can pack it away. Press ‘U’. It costs 1 AP.
steps.then: The parachute is gone, and Barrow has 3 AP left of his 4.

steps.tell: Why pack it? Move the mouse onto the ‘PATROL’ umpire on the road.
steps.then: The dotted line is the beat the patrol walks. A patrol finds any parachute it walks onto or beside, and each one found adds 1 to the alert. The second parachute lies right beside that beat.

steps.tell: Any man can pack any parachute. Move Barrow onto the one Vance left: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: Barrow is standing on Vance's parachute. The 2 hexes of grass cost 2 AP, and he has 1 left.

steps.tell: Pack this one too. Press ‘U’: his last AP.
steps.then: Both are packed, and the patrol will find nothing. That is the choice after every drop: packing costs AP, and a parachute left lying costs alert when it is found.

steps.tell: Each counter on the map is one of your men. Click Dutch.
steps.then: Dutch is selected. The dots on his counter are his action points (AP): he has 3 each turn. Everything a man does is paid for in AP.

steps.tell: Open grass costs 1 AP a hex. Move the mouse onto the ringed hex to see the path and what it costs, then click it.
steps.then: He walked 2 hexes of grass and spent 2 AP. 1 dot is left on his counter.

steps.tell: AP not used are lost when the turn ends. Press ‘SPACE’, or click END TURN.
steps.then: A new turn. Every man starts it with all his AP again: Dutch has 3.

steps.say: A HEDGE COSTS TWO. GO THERE.
steps.tell: Rough ground costs more. A hedge is 2 AP a hex. Click the ringed hex.
steps.then: 1 hex of hedge cost 2 AP. In return it hides him far better than open grass does.

steps.tell: Ground does two things: it costs AP to cross, and it gives cover. Click Vance.
steps.then: Vance is selected. He is a scout, with 4 AP.

steps.tell: Move the mouse onto the ringed hex of wood.
steps.then: The box under the map names the ground at the right of its top line. A wood is Move 2, which is 2 AP a hex, and heavy cover. The number on each hex of the path is the AP spent by the time he gets there.

steps.tell: Now move the mouse onto the ringed hex of marsh.
steps.then: Marsh is Move 3 and only light cover: slow to cross, and not much to hide in.

steps.tell: Grass and road are 1 AP a hex, and neither gives any cover. Move him onto the road by the bridge: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: 2 hexes for 2 AP. He has 2 left.

steps.tell: Nobody can walk through water. The only way over the brook on foot is the bridge. Click the ringed hex on the far bank.
steps.then: Over the bridge for his last 2 AP. A bridge is 1 AP a hex, like the road, and gives no cover.

steps.tell: The ‘SENTRY’ umpire by the brook is looking this way. Click Fitch.
steps.then: The faint red wedge in front of the sentry is what he can see. With a man selected, the ground he can reach is tinted: red where he would be spotted, blue where he would not.

steps.tell: Move the mouse onto the ringed hex.
steps.then: The box under the map says why it is red. The dots are how well he would be seen there: at 3 he is spotted. Open grass takes nothing off.

steps.tell: A hedge is heavy cover and takes 2 dots off. Move Fitch into it: click the ringed hex. If you end the turn on red ground instead, the umpire blows his whistle and the step starts again.
steps.then: In the hedge he is 1 dot of 3: not enough to be spotted.

steps.tell: Going to ground makes him harder still to see. Press ‘H’ for ‘Hide’: 1 AP, and it ends his turn.
steps.then: Fitch is hidden, marked on his counter: 1 dot fewer. He stays hidden until he next spends AP.

steps.tell: The garrison looks only when the turn ends, never before. Press ‘SPACE’.
steps.then: The umpire looked, and saw nobody.

steps.say: NOW GET IT WRONG. STEP OUT.
steps.tell: Now see what being seen does. Move Fitch out onto the red ground: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: He is standing in plain view, and nothing has happened. A man is only seen when the turn ends.

steps.tell: End the turn, and the umpire will see him.
steps.then: Seen. The alert went up by 1. Fitch is in contact, marked on his counter, and the umpire is facing him. A man in contact who is seen again is shot.

steps.say: BREAK CONTACT. BACK TO THE HEDGE.
steps.tell: He has this one turn to get out of sight. Green ground is where he would not be seen. Click the ringed hex.
steps.then: He is back in the hedge, where the umpire cannot make him out.

steps.tell: End the turn.
steps.then: The umpire looked and saw nobody. Contact is broken, and the mark is gone from Fitch's counter.

steps.tell: Two umpires are out: a ‘PATROL’ on the road west of the brook, and a ‘SENTRY’ beyond Nunn's hedge. Click Nunn.
steps.then: Nunn is selected. The garrison is never hidden, and it does nothing the map has not shown first. Watching it is how a raid is planned.

steps.tell: Move the mouse onto the ‘PATROL’ umpire, on the road west of the bridge.
steps.then: The dotted line is its beat: it walks there and back. The solid wedge is what it sees now, up to 3 hexes. The dashed wedge is the way it will face next turn. ‘R’ shows every beat at once.

steps.tell: A sentry never leaves his post: he only turns. Move the mouse onto the ringed hex in front of this one.
steps.then: Red. The sentry looks west over this grass, and Nunn would be seen there.

steps.tell: A thrown stone turns a sentry's head. Press ‘T’ for ‘Throw’, then click the ringed hex behind him.
steps.then: The stone cost 1 AP and added 1 to the alert. Every sentry within 3 hexes of where it landed has turned to look, at once. A stone can be thrown up to 3 hexes.

steps.tell: The grass is no longer red. He looks away only until this turn ends. Nunn has 2 AP left: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: Nunn is standing on ground the sentry was watching a moment ago.

steps.tell: End the turn.
steps.then: The umpire looked while he was still facing the stone, and did not see Nunn. Now he has turned back. A stone buys one turn: next turn Nunn must be gone from there, or under cover.

steps.tell: The knife is silent, and any man can use it. Click Vance.
steps.then: A knife needs the man beside the enemy and behind him, and not seen. This ‘SENTRY’ umpire faces east, away from Vance.

steps.tell: Move Vance into the hedge behind the umpire: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: Vance is beside the umpire and behind him, unseen. But the knife takes a man's whole turn: he must not have spent any AP, and the hedge cost him 2.

steps.tell: So he waits. End the turn.
steps.then: A new turn, and Vance has spent nothing. The knife mark on the umpire's counter says Vance could use it now.

steps.tell: Press ‘N’, then click the umpire.
steps.then: Silent: no noise and no alert. It leaves a body, and a body the garrison finds adds 1 to the alert.

steps.tell: Only a gunner can open fire on an enemy who has not seen him. Click Speers.
steps.then: Speers is a gunner. He can fire at an enemy within 2 hexes with a clear line to him: the umpire on the track, who has his back turned.

steps.tell: Press ‘S’ for ‘Suppress’, then click the umpire. It costs 2 AP.
steps.then: The umpire has his head down: he will see nobody and shoot nobody when this turn ends. It was gunfire: 2 alert (1 from Speers, whose skill is a Cool Head), and patrols within 5 hexes come to look. Speers has 1 AP left, and a kill costs 2.

steps.tell: One gunner needs two turns to kill; two gunners can do it in one. End the turn.
steps.then: A new turn. The suppressed umpire saw nothing, and Speers has his 3 AP again.

steps.tell: An enemy who was suppressed last turn can be killed. Press ‘K’ for ‘Kill’, then click the umpire. It costs 2 AP.
steps.then: One silenced shot: heard only 2 hexes away, 1 alert (none from Speers). It never misses, and it leaves a body.

steps.tell: A man who isn't a gunner cannot fire first. But a man who has been seen can fire back. Click Fitch.
steps.then: Fitch is on open grass in front of this ‘SENTRY’ umpire. When the turn ends he will be seen.

steps.tell: Let him be seen. End the turn.
steps.then: Fitch has been seen and is in contact: the umpire has him in his sights. If that umpire sees him again when this turn ends, Fitch is shot.

steps.tell: For a man who isn't a gunner, ‘S’ is ‘Fire back’. Press it, then click the umpire who has seen him. It costs 2 AP.
steps.then: The umpire's head is down. It was gunfire, so 2 alert. Fitch has 1 AP left to move with.

steps.tell: End the turn.
steps.then: The umpire had his head down and saw nobody: Fitch was not shot, and contact is broken. Firing back buys one turn, and costs alert.

steps.tell: On some missions the charges come down in canisters, and have to be fetched. Click Barrow.
steps.then: The canister on the grass beside Barrow holds 2 charges. Any man standing on it can take one.

steps.tell: Move Barrow onto the canister: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: Barrow is standing on the canister, with 3 AP left of his 4.

steps.tell: Press ‘P’ to pick up a charge. It costs 1 AP.
steps.then: Barrow carries a charge. He is a scout and did not jump with one, so its weight costs him 1 AP in every turn he carries it: he has 1 AP left, not 2. A sapper carries one at full pace.

steps.tell: Passing a charge costs 2 AP, and he has 1. End the turn.
steps.then: A new turn, and Barrow has 3 AP, not his 4: the weight of the charge.

steps.tell: So give it to a sapper. Fitch is beside him: press ‘E’ to pass it. With more than one man beside him, he would then click the one to have it.
steps.then: Fitch has the charge. Passing cost Barrow 2 AP and Fitch nothing, and Barrow has his 4 AP again next turn. One charge is still in the canister: a patrol finds a canister as it does a parachute, until it is empty.

steps.tell: A target is destroyed by charges set on its charge points. Click Nunn.
steps.then: The two hexes outlined in dashed red beside the Training Bridge are its charge points. The bridge wants 2 charges, one on each. Nunn carries one; a second charge lies at the far point.

steps.tell: A charge is set from a charge point. Move Nunn onto the nearer one: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: Nunn is on a charge point, with 2 AP left. Now he can set it: the ‘Charge’ button is lit.

steps.tell: Press ‘C’. The tin of time pencils opens: each is a timer, counted in turns with this turn as the first. Pick the 4, then press SET. It costs 1 AP.
steps.then: The charge is set and burning. It goes off at the end of turn 4, and kills any man within 1 hex of it then.

steps.tell: The other point is 2 hexes off, and he has 1 AP. End the turn.
steps.then: Turn 2. The first charge has one turn less to burn.

steps.tell: Move Nunn to the other charge point: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: Nunn is on the second point, standing on the charge left there, with 1 AP.

steps.tell: Press ‘P’ to pick up the charge at his feet: his last AP.
steps.then: Nunn carries it. He will set it next turn.

steps.tell: End the turn.
steps.then: Turn 3. The first charge goes off at the end of turn 4.

steps.tell: Set this one to go off with the first, at the end of turn 4. That is 2 turns from now: press ‘C’, pick the 2, then SET.
steps.then: Both charges will go off together at the end of turn 4. Nunn is standing on one of them, with 2 AP left.

steps.tell: Get him out of the blast. Move Nunn to the ringed hex, 2 hexes from the charge.
steps.then: Nunn is clear: more than 1 hex from both charges.

steps.tell: Now wait for it. Press Space to end turn 3, and again to end turn 4.
steps.then: The Training Bridge is down. An explosion is heard everywhere and adds 3 to the alert. Charges on one target that go off in the same turn are one explosion, which is why the two timers were matched.

steps.tell: Sgt. Holloway, ‘Dutch’, leads the stick, and his orders are worth AP. Click Dutch.
steps.then: The dashed blue line is how far his orders carry: 2 hexes. When a turn starts, a man inside it has 1 AP more, and a man beside Dutch 2 more. Fitch is 3 hexes off.

steps.tell: Move Dutch beside Fitch: click the ringed hex.
steps.then: Dutch is beside Fitch. Orders are given when a turn starts, so Fitch still has his 3 AP.

steps.tell: End the turn.
steps.then: Fitch has 5 AP, not 3: the dots on his counter. The 2 blue chevrons on it are Dutch's orders.

steps.tell: Now use them. Click Fitch.
steps.then: Fitch is selected, with 5 AP. The ‘SENTRY’ umpire beyond the hedge is looking this way.

steps.tell: The ringed hex is 4 AP away: further than Fitch could go on his own 3. It is red, and he will be seen there. Today that is the lesson. Click it.
steps.then: Fitch is beside the umpire, in plain view, with 1 AP left.

steps.tell: End the turn.
steps.then: The umpire has turned to face Fitch. Fitch is seen and in contact, and the alert is Suspicious. Seen again when this turn ends, he would be shot.

steps.tell: The leader carries the radio, and can call a diversion. In a mission it is an RAF raid on the town. Today it is the instructor's thunderflash. Press ‘D’, or click its button beside the dial. It costs no AP.
steps.then: The umpire has turned away, back to his post. The alert has dropped one state, to Calm, and Fitch is out of contact. The radio can be used once in a mission, and only while the leader is alive.

steps.say: EACH MAN HAS A SKILL. PRESS NEXT.
steps.tell: Every man has a skill of his own. It is printed on his row in the list, with what it does in numbers. This lesson uses two of them.
Click Fitch, by the Training Bridge.
steps.then: Fitch is a sapper, standing on a charge point with a charge. His skill is Quick Work: setting a charge costs him no AP.

steps.tell: Set his charge: press ‘C’, pick the 4, then SET.
steps.then: The charge is set, and Fitch still has all 3 of his AP. It costs any other man 1.

steps.tell: The ‘SENTRY’ umpire across the brook is looking west. Move the mouse onto the ringed hex in front of him.
steps.then: Red. Fitch would be spotted there, and so would any man but one.

steps.tell: Now click Vance, on the grass to the west.
steps.then: For Vance the same hex is not red. His skill is Cat's Eyes: he is 1 dot harder to see than anyone else, harder even than Barrow, the other scout.

steps.tell: Move Vance onto the ringed hex.
steps.then: Vance is on open grass, 2 hexes in front of the umpire, with 2 AP left.

steps.tell: End the turn, and see whether the umpire spots him.
steps.then:
The umpire looked, and did not see him.
The other men's skills: Dutch's charges go off a turn sooner (Steady Hands). Barrow loses no turn landing in a wood or a marsh (Treetops). Speers's gunfire adds 1 less to the alert (Cool Head). Nunn, a gunner, jumps with a charge (Ox).

steps.tell: A raid is not over until the men are out. Click Barrow.
steps.then: The way out is marked on every map. Here it is the gate, at the foot of the lane Barrow is standing on. A man who ends a move on it is out.

steps.tell: A mission ends at dawn, on its last turn. A man still on the map at dawn is left behind. Every man out adds to the score, and more if he was never hit.
Send Barrow out: click the ringed hex at the gate. The lane is 1 AP a hex.
steps.then: Barrow is out, and he cannot come back. If the last man goes out with the job not done, that is a withdrawal, and the game asks first whether you are sure. So: the job, then the gate, before dawn.

steps.tell: The dial is the whole garrison's mood, counted in points. Calm is 0 and 1, Suspicious from 2, Alert from 4, Alarmed from 7. Today it stands at 1: Calm.
Click Nunn.
steps.then: The ‘SENTRY’ umpire on the road is looking this way. While the garrison is Calm he sees 3 hexes: the red wedge.

steps.tell: Move the mouse onto the ringed hex, 4 hexes in front of the umpire.
steps.then: Not red. It is 1 hex further than he sees.

steps.tell: Now raise the alert. A thrown stone adds 1. Press ‘T’, then click the ringed hex behind Nunn.
steps.then: A red pip flew from the stone to the dial, which now reads Suspicious. A Suspicious garrison sees 1 hex further: the umpire's wedge has grown.

steps.tell: Move the mouse onto the same ringed hex again.
steps.then: Red now. Nunn has not moved and nor has the umpire: only the dial.

steps.tell: A man seen, a parachute or a body found, a stone: 1 each. Gunfire 2. An explosion 3. At Alert the garrison also looks harder and hears further. At Alarmed every patrol hunts the last place a man was seen.
Time. After 4 turns with nothing raised and nobody seen, it drops to the start of the state below. Once a charge has gone off it never drops below Suspicious.
Nunn has been hit. Click Barrow, beside him.
steps.then: A wounded man has 1 AP a turn and cannot carry a charge, and a second hit kills him. A man beside him can dress the wound. It takes that man's whole turn: he must not have spent any AP.

steps.tell: Press ‘A’ for ‘Aid’, then click Nunn.
steps.then: The wound is dressed. It took all 4 of Barrow's AP.

steps.tell: End the turn.
steps.then: Nunn has his 3 AP again, and can carry a charge. The wound is dressed, not healed: one more hit still kills him, and a man who gets out wounded scores less.

steps.tell: The passing-out exercise: a whole raid, and nobody to tell you what to click. Blow the Training Bridge, then get all six men out by the gate. First, choose the drop run and jump.

All six are down. The Training Bridge wants 2 charges, one on each of its charge points, and 2 umpires are watching it. After that, all six men out by the gate.
If the umpire's whistle stops you, the exercise goes back to its last checkpoint. This is the first.

steps.say: SET THE SECOND CHARGE. GET CLEAR.
steps.tell: CHECKPOINT. The first charge is set and burning. Set the second, and have every man more than 1 hex from both when they go off.
CHECKPOINT. The Training Bridge is down. Now get all six men out by the gate.
